Motion passed by the following vote:

BOARD OF TRUSTEES REPORTS

2. CHAIRPERSON REPORT

Chairperson Domier expressed his gratitude for the service that the Board provides the community.
He thanked Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth for her guidance, leadership, years of service, wisdom,
and friendship. He mentioned that his overall goal is to ensure that all stakeholders work together
so that the Crowell Public Library continues to enrich the community. In preparation for his new
role, he reviewed the handbook for commissions, boards, and committees and noted a passage he
found helpful. The passage read that each member should show respect for other’s viewpoints, allow

others adequate time to present their views before making comments, be open and honest, and
strive to minimize political action among members. He also quoted an author who said politeness is
not the same as kindness. He hopes that the Board continues to speak their minds respectfully.
During the agenda setting meeting last Monday, he noted how Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth said
that this is a time of change and there are opportunities as a result of these changes. In 2022,
Chairperson Domier hopes for better coordination between the Board and the two Library support
groups, the Friends and the Foundation. He also hopes that a consensus can be made related to the
Board’s responsibilities and that the strategic plan can be clarified and implemented. He hopes to be
a resource for Director Johnson as she staffs the Librarian position and hopes to strengthen the
Board by adding two alternate members.

3. TRUSTEE REPORTS

Trustee Mollno shared her agreement with Chairperson Domier’s request to get the alternate
positions filled. She noted the importance of alternates, as they help the Board meet quorum and
prevent cancellation of any meetings.

Trustee Chien shared that she enjoyed what Chairperson Domier said in his Chairperson Report.

4. CRAIN ART GALLERY REPORT

Trustee Mollno reported that Sean Kirkpatrick’s exhibit came down at the end of October. He sold
one painting for $200 and donated $40 to the Library. She noted that donations from the artists are
voluntary, but they recommend a donation of 10%, which she believes is an exceptional deal since
most galleries take upwards of 50% of the sale price. She stated that Marian Fortunati’s work went
up right after Kirkpatrick’s exhibit was taken down. Fortunati’s work will be up through January 2.
Trustee Mollno also reported attending the reception held for Marian Fortunati on November 20.
She noted that it was very nicely attended and many people were chatting with Fortunati and asking
questions. She noted that the calendar for 2022 is still a work in progress. She added that several
virtual artists are interested in doing an in person exhibit in 2022. The next artist to have their work
displayed may be Marie McDuffie.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if there are any expenses related to the Crain Art Gallery.
Trustee Mollno responded that there are no upcoming expenses that she knows of since Staff have
not expressed any needs at this time.

5. MARKETING AND PUBLICITY LIAISON REPORT

Chairperson Domier suggested that this report be discontinued for the next year since there haven’t
been any meetings and any information will be included in his Chairperson Report or in Director
Johnson’s report.

6. BUDGET AND CIP LIAISON REPORT

Trustee Chien reported that her and Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth met with Management Analyst
Shigenaga last week. Trustee Chien shared that they talked about donations and how the Board likes
to see the transactions. She noted that they care a lot about tracking the donations since they want
to be responsible with the contributions received from the community.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that the CIP portion of the report is redundant at this point
since there are no CIP projects this year. She then thanked Management Analyst Shigenaga for
meeting with herself and Trustee Chien last week.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that Mayor Ude sent the Board an email regarding a change
in the financial reports that the Board receives and requested that Mayor Ude explain it in more
detail. Mayor Ude started off saying that part of the reason for the change is to try to save Staff time.
He noted that the City is really understaffed in a lot of areas. He continued to say that several Staff
provide financial oversight to the budget. Mayor Ude recommended that moving to a quarterly
review, in a summary mode, would be a healthy step. He added that the financials on the Library
side don’t change a lot; most of the changes observed are due to staffing.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth recalled the executive summary financial reports that Director
Johnson included last month in her report. She noted how on the Budget Monitor there are about
65-line items, but on the executive summary financial reports there are 7-line items. She did
acknowledge that the Board does not need all the detail provided in the Budget Monitor, but doesn’t
believe the executive summary quite does it. She continued that she recognizes that the Board’s
role is to advise the Council, but is worried that she won’t be able to provide the Council with good
advice just based on the executive summary reports. She stated that there needs to be something
in between the Budget Monitor and the executive summary financial reports that the Board can
receive. She went on to say that she trusts the Staff assigned to oversee the budget, but with the
high turnover in the past years, it has been tough to ensure nothing slips between the cracks. She
mentioned how she brought a donation to Management Analyst Shigenaga’s attention that doesn’t
appear on last year’s Donation Monitor. She recommended meeting to see how the Budget Monitor
can be modified and to also talk about the frequency of the report. She is also very interested in the
Donation Monitor and seeing if it is the best tool to track donations.

Mayor Ude added that when City develops the budget, there is much detail. However, when actual
financials are presented, they are in summary form and variances are presented with notes similar
to what was done in the executive summary financial reports. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted
that the executive summary reports do not include donations. Mayor Ude responded that
Management Analyst Shigenaga can create a schedule for donations. He added that the Board most
likely does not need the line item detail on a monthly basis. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted
that on the Budget Monitor, many expenditures are related to donations, which are also found in
the Donations Monitor. That is the information she would really like to see moving forward. She
added that about a year ago, they talked about changing the approach to donations in the budget
process. This conversation was never finished and nothing ever came of it. She asked why the City
is paying for Other Contract Services, Materials & Supplies, etc. when the Friends donate so much
money. She added that the Library heavily relies upon donations, which can get tough during times
like when the Friends couldn’t raise money. She recommended building the budget without any
donations in it, and then asking different groups to give donations for specific items.

Mayor Ude asked what the annual budgeted amount of donations is. Management Analyst Shigenaga
responded that in the current fiscal year, there is $21,000 budgeted in the various donation line
items. Mayor Ude noted that the Library’s entire budget is around $1,500,000. Vice Chairperson

Hollingsworth asked why the donations are used on such basic kinds of expenditures. She added
that we have a responsibility to the donors to spend the reserve funds before we go asking for more
money. She noted how she attended the Chinese Club gala the other weekend and thanked them
for their donation, but has no idea if we’ve spent the money yet. She would at least like to know a
plan to spend it, to make sure it is in the way the donor wants. She noted that if the donations were
not used from one year to the next, they were sucked up for general use. She would like unspent
donations to be set aside for the same purpose.

Mayor Ude understood the issues to be really related to the donations. He recommended that
Director Johnson and Management Analyst Shigenaga work to come up with a schedule of donations
and their related expenditures to be presented to the Board on a quarterly basis. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth asked Mayor Ude on his opinion of seeing a budget built not relying on donations and
he responded that he is indifferent since the amount of donations compared to the entire Library’s
budget is not a big number.

Trustee Mollno agreed with everything Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth said, but added that there
are sections of the Budget Monitor that the Board doesn’t necessarily need. She noted that she has
faith in Staff putting the Monitors together. She said that compared to the Staff monitoring the
budget, the Trustees are primary interested in the Library. She has no problem making the Budget
Monitor shorter by removing some line items, but she does take offense when saying the $21,000
in donations does not matter. Mayor Ude noted that he didn’t say it doesn’t matter. He meant to
say that in the scheme of the entire budget, $20,000 is not as big of a number. He suggested that
Board let Director Johnson and Management Analyst Shigenaga come back with a new donation
report. He noted that on the Budget Monitors, the Board should be looking at the variances to
effectively manage the financial aspect of the City. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth responded that
she likes Mayor Ude’s idea of letting Director Johnson and Management Analyst Shigenaga prepare
a new report for further discussion in January. She added that on the Quarterly Reports, she would
like to see the difference between program and book purchases in Adult and Children’s Services.
She also requested that the other Trustees compare the Budget Monitor and the Quarterly Report
to see what else they would like to see in a new report.

Mayor Ude stated that Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth’s requests are healthy additions to the
schedules. Chairperson Domier added that the current Budget Monitor is so detailed and extensive
that it just becomes noise and difficult to pay attention to what is important. He also mentioned that
when we ask for donations for something specific and it doesn’t get spent the way we said it would,
it makes us look bad as the people requesting the money. Trustee Derry agreed. Mayor Ude thinks
that the Board is making its way towards a healthy operating dashboard, by focusing on what actually
moves the needle, similar to what the Council receives on each department. Trustee Derry agrees
that the Board should focus on what moves the Library forward.

Director Johnson thanked Mayor Ude for facilitating this discussion. She appreciated the background
knowledge on the challenges around the tracking of donations and ensuring that donations are spent
for their intended use. She believes it is our obligation to report on that, but isn’t sure that the
existing reports are the best way of doing so. She mentioned that she has not been able to meet
with Finance Director, Paul Chung, to be able to better understand the restricted donations reserve
fund. This includes understanding why there is a balance and if there is a threshold that needs to be

maintained. She also mentioned the idea of a working meeting to Chairperson Domier and Vice
Chairperson Hollingsworth along with Management Analyst Shigenaga obtain the historic
perspective, talk about the clarifying questions, and improve the tools going forward.

Management Analyst Shigenaga experienced technical difficulties with Zoom and could not stop
screen sharing. In the meantime, Trustee Mollno provided some background on the restricted
donations reserve fund. She noted that for the Crain Art Gallery, the money in the reserve fund is
money that has accumulated over the years form artists. In the past, it had been difficult to track
down the funds. She had to work with City Staff to make sure donations did not get absorbed into
the General Fund. She explained that the $12,000 balance is for when they need to spend money
on something for the Art Gallery. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth added that in 2018, the Library
had received $50,000 in donations and the City’s Finance policy was “use it or lose it.” She added
that they had to work with the City’s Finance Director to create with a Donation Policy that City
Council adopted in September 2018. In addition, she noted that the Library created its own policy
for steps after receiving a donation, which lives on the Library’s website. She noted that Accounting
Manager, Mark Siegfried, helped find the donations that were not accrued over the years. She
mentioned her hope that the $62,000 in restricted donations reserve fund can be spent out because
she believes it is disingenuous to ask for donations when we have unspent donation money. Mayor
Ude added that he thinks there should be a different bank account for the Library donations and
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that that is the case now, but wasn’t back in 2018. Director
Johnson noted that she will review the City’s Donation Policy and agreed that it is odd to receive
donations, but not use them in a timely manner and instead allow the donations to build up in a big
reserve like a safety net. She noted that she will do a lot of research to come up to speed on this.

Chairperson Domier highlighted that there is a lot of experience in this group, which has allowed
them to inform the new Staff. He added that Mayor Ude ran on platform of transparency, so better
documenting our numbers accurately is the goal. Mayor Ude added that he is understanding that the
Board wants to see when the donations are coming in, what is it being spent on, and verifying that
it is not lost over the fiscal years. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if the money in the reserve
fund from the City can be given to the Foundation to put into the endowment fund. Trustee Mollno
added that the money she is referencing is not all of the Foundation’s money; there is also Crain Art
Gallery money lumped in there. Mayor Ude was unsure and recommended that Director Johnson
talk to Director Chung. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth recommended also utilizing Accounting
Manager Siegfried. Director Johnson noted that the City will be kicking off budget in a month or
two and will add this to her list of items to address. She also added that she will be working with
Management Analyst Shigenaga on preparing a 3rd quarter report and appreciated the opportunity
to hear the priorities of the Board. Trustee Mollno added that she should keep in mind that the
$21,000 budgeted revenue through donations is an anomaly due to COVID-19. In years prior to
COVID-19, the donation revenue were 3-5 times that amount. Director Johnson understood and
said she will do some historical research. Chairperson Domier added that, like Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth mentioned, donations should not be thought of when the Library’s budget is
developed to cover things like the interior painting of the Library. He continued and said that
donations should be used for things like technology, books, etc. Director Johnson understood that
donations should support day to day operational needs.

7. SAN MARINO CENTER RENOVATION UPDATE REPORT

Chairperson Domier reported no meeting had occurred. Mayor Ude added that it is very close to
being able to go out to bid. He mentioned that Director Throne has prescreened three contractors
that are qualified to do the work and the drawings have gone through plan checks. Director Johnson
added that at the last meeting, Trustee Mollno brought up that there were some misconceptions
about the plan for the facility once renovated. She reached out to Director Throne to write an
article to appear in the Winter Activities Guide, which will include renderings and an update on
where the project sits.

ADMINISTRATIVE BUSINESS

8. DIRECTOR AND CITY LIBRARIAN REPORT

Director Johnson noted Acting City Librarian Plumley is also on the call. She said that there are
several critical positions that need to be filled to have highly responsive Library operations. Two full
time positions are in the recruitment phase right now: City Librarian and Adult Services Librarian II.
She stated that the City Librarian recruitment closed on Monday after receiving 63 applications and
there are plans for first-round interviews on November 29, with second and third round interviews
in the first and second week of December. She noted that the Adult Services Librarian II job posting
is being finalized and should be posted today. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked that if the
Library will be back to pre-pandemic staffing levels after getting the two full time positions filled.
Director Johnson noted that she hopes to get the two full time positions filled and settled by end of
February. She added that another full time Librarian is going on maternity leave from February –
May, so there will continue to be capacity issues. Acting City Librarian Plumley added that some
hiring was done when the Library opened back up to the public. He explained that staffing levels are
back up to pre-pandemic levels. Director Johnson added that we are losing a part time Librarian in
December. Acting City Librarian Plumley said that there are plans to recruit for that position.

Director Johnson asked if there were any questions related to the San Marino Unified School District
agreement. She explained that the District no longer has a Librarian and wants to partner with
Crowell Public Library to fill that role. She noted that the City Attorney and City Manager are
currently reviewing the agreement.

She continued to say that all Community Services Staff are vaccinated and the requirement for
volunteers has been rolled out verbally. She noted that she is working with the Friends of the Library
to make sure that any volunteers on site are fully vaccinated. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth added
that the Board needs to be fully vaccinated before resuming in person meetings. Director Johnson
clarified that City Council will let us know when it is approved to return to in person meetings. Vice
Chairperson Hollingsworth asked Trustee Derry how she feels about meeting in person. Trustee
Derry responded that she would love to see in person meetings and can’t imagine any of the Board
Members not being fully vaccinated.

Director Johnson noted that City Clerk, Christina Baker, will be providing a cheat sheet flyer on the
Brown Act. She asked if a virtual training is still needed. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth said that
they can wait to see the flyer before requesting a training. She noted that the clarification most
needed is serial and electronic communication. Trustee Mollno added that when she started on the

Board, the City Attorney attended a meeting and provided information on the Brown Act. She
requested that the training be provided most efficiently. Chairperson Domier added that since the
Board will be losing two members in June, it would be a good idea to provide this training to the
new members as well. Trustee Mollno added that it would be nice to have the two Alternate
positions filled and for them to sit through the training as well. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth said
that a flyer would be great. Director Johnson asked if a facilitated training is necessary and decided
that she will defer to Chairperson Domier for this.

Director Johnson continued that the old Management Analyst’s Report will now be included in the
Director’s Report. She noted that City Staff are trying to streamline the reporting process and
ensure that the level of reporting meets the expectations of the Board. Any highlights and budget
notes to date will be provided for both the operating budget and the donation budget. She asked
about the $40 donation from the artist that Trustee Mollno brought up earlier. Trustee Mollno
added that she isn’t sure that Staff had received and processed the check just yet, as this was very
recent. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked how the Restricted Donations Reserve Fund Balance
increased by $10,000 in the few days since the last meeting. Management Analyst Shigenaga
responded that after meeting with Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth, she reached out to the Finance
Department to see how she could get those updated numbers, since they had not been updated
since the prior fiscal year. The numbers shown today are the updated balances as of the end of the
last fiscal year. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked how much the balance increased and
Management Analyst Shigenaga did not know off the top of her head. They agreed to meet separately
to talk about it. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked about the second donation received from
the Chinese Club last year. Management Analyst Shigenaga responded that she had not had the time
to look into that just yet. Director Johnson commended Management Analyst Shigenaga for
completing good research and getting her arms around the financials. She noted that internal
processes are not easy to navigate around, but they will continue to work with Finance to make
sure they know how to do things.

Director Johnson mentioned reaching out to the San Marino Public Library Foundation and Friends
of the Library to get updates. She also mentioned the list of upcoming events that the Board can
attend or participate in. She highlighted the asterisk, which connotates that it is a Recreation led
event.

She explained that the next section highlights operational and programming updates. Vice
Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that there was an idea of the City Council meeting in the Barth
Room while the San Marino Center goes under renovations. She asked if they added another
monitor, which is something that Council will need in order to have meetings in that room. Acting
City Librarian Plumley noted that the work done recently was repairs and is unsure of the status of
an additional monitor. Director Johnson noted that she hasn’t attended any renovation task force
meetings yet, but will ask this question at the next meeting. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth said
that she will look at her notes to see if she can find the proposal to gain some insight on it. She
added that in the interest of saving Staff time, the Board doesn’t need to know about the facility
maintenance work orders. She is mainly interested in the pending projects. Director Johnson noted
that they do affect customer service and programming. Mayor Ude recommended keeping the
discussion at a strategic level. He continued that given reserve balance of $62,000 and the revenue
budget of $21,000, the Board should have a wish list of projects that could really move the needle

in terms of the performance of the Library. Chairperson Domier and Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth agreed. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that pre-pandemic, the Friends usually
donated $50,000. She noted that the $21,000 of revenue is budgeted to be spent, so nothing will

NEW BUSINESS

9. BOARD OF TRUSTEES MEETING SCHEDULE FOR 2022

Chairperson Domier noted in preparation for this meeting, there was discussion about whether to
keep the March joint meeting with City Council on the calendar. He noted that it is kept there as a
placeholder. He asked if there is any discussion. Trustee Mollno liked keeping the joint meeting date
on the list, but wanted to express her displeasure with the meeting in July and closing in August. She
noted that this was dictated by Council, but thinks it makes no sense since the facility works
especially for children. She thinks that the Board should be dark in July and open in August when
the schools are open. She continued to say that if the Library is up and running in August, the
Trustees should be there to do their part. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth agreed with Trustee
Mollno. She added that school started this year on August 11. By meeting at the end of July, the
Board heard about what the Library had planned for the opening of school. She would also like the
Board be open to having an August meeting should it be necessary as the Library moves into an
agreement with the school district. Trustee Mollno added that opening the possibility of an August
meeting is a good idea. She clarified that her concern with July is that there could be a meeting
without a quorum. Since the Board is trying to attract Trustees with younger kids, July would be the
last month for them to go on vacation, which could cause the lack of quorum. Chairperson Domier
agreed that it makes more sense to have a meeting in July and not in August since the school district
seems to move the start date up earlier each year. He does like the idea of potentially having an
August meeting if necessary.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth moved, seconded by Trustee Derry, to submit this as written for
the calendar for 2022 to the City Manager.

Trustee Mollno mentioned an Old Business item that she would like to see on one of the next

 SUBJECT:  STATUS UPDATE ON TRUSTEE & ALTERNATE RECRUITMENTS

BACKGROUND

The Library Board of Trustees consists of five (5) regular members and two (2) alternates. Board
members are appointed by the City Council to serve up to two (2) consecutive three (3) year
terms. One alternate position has been vacant since late 2020 and the other alternate position
has been vacant since late 2021. The Board has expressed interest in filling the two alternate
positions. In addition, two (2) regular members are terming out at the end of May.

At the request of the Chairperson Domier, Staff reached out to the City Clerk to gain some
insight on the plans to fill the two (2) alternate position vacancies and the two (2) impending
regular member vacancies.

DISCUSSION

Regarding the impending regular member vacancies, City Clerk Baker shared that the annual
recruitment for the terms ending this year will begin in April. The goal is to post the recruitment
notice on April 4, and per the Municipal Code, the notice needs to be posted for at least twenty
(20) days. After the recruitment closes, the applications will be reviewed and then the Council
liaisons will be consulted to see how they would like to move forward. This step will most likely
include interviews with the applicants. Finally, the Council liaisons would make the
recommendation to the full City Council of the appointments. This is likely be on the City Council
agenda in either May or June depending on how the application and interview process goes. This
recruitment will be for all of the City’s boards and commissions so coordinating schedules with
the various Council liaisons for the interviews may impact the timeline.

Regarding the alternate position vacancies, City Clerk Baker reached out to the Council liaisons
to see if they wanted to start the alternate position recruitments now or hold off to have the
recruitments at the same time as the annual recruitment for the regular members. Vice Mayor
Talt shared that if the Board feels hamstrung from the empty alternate positions, then the
recruitments can be held now. If the recruitment occurs now, given the posting requirements

  30 of 32
 and interview process, the alternate recruitments would wrap up around the time that the regular
member recruitments begins. City Clerk Baker shared a concern that the people who apply for
the alternate positions would likely apply for the regular member positions, which may get a bit
confusing for the applicants.

City Clerk Baker recommended Staff to share the above options with the Board and to obtain
feedback as to how to move forward.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Board review, comment, and provide feedback, which will be
forwarded to the City Clerk, related to an all-inclusive recruitment in April 2022 or an earlier
recruitment specific to the alternate positions.

Next, she shared the revised list of Council Delegates and Alternates. She highlighted that the

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked for an update on the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)

need to go to Council, but if it needs updating, the Board is open to assisting. Her request for the
